init.description: Sets up a project for impeccable. Runs a multi-round discovery interview when context is missing and writes PRODUCT.md (strategic: users, brand, principles); offers DESIGN.md (visual: colors, typography, components) when code exists; pre-configures live mode; then recommends the best commands to run next. Every other command reads these files before doing work. Use once per project.

teach.description: Explain and establish the durable product context Melzi needs before it designs. Uses the init playbook to clarify users, purpose, principles, platform, and working constraints, then writes PRODUCT.md with the user. Use when the user asks Melzi to teach them the setup or product-context method.

document.description: Generate a DESIGN.md file that captures the current visual system, or consolidate repeated components and tokens into that system in Extract mode. Reads the codebase, stages portable Google Stitch tokens, records qualitative rules, migrates shared implementations when requested, and writes the sidecar used by the live panel.

identity.description: Guides a visual identity session from scratch, an existing project, an admired brand, or learned taste, including the complete production-mark workflow. It derives accessible colour, type, and spacing tokens from rendered choices, constructs and validates editable marks with lineage and proof, joins an adopted mark to the backed-up personal signature, and verifies DESIGN.md binding and mark propagation.

live.description: Interactive live variant mode. Select elements in the browser, pick a design action, and get AI-generated HTML+CSS variants hot-swapped via HMR. Requires a running dev server. Use when you want to visually experiment with design alternatives in real time.

generate.description: Agent-driven live variant generation. Boots live mode, finds the named element on the open page, scrolls the browser to it, and delivers N variants in the requested direction for the user to cycle and accept. Use for requests that name an element and a direction, like 'generate 3 bold variants of the pricing cards', skipping manual element picking.

animate.description: Review a feature and enhance it with purposeful animations, micro-interactions, and motion effects that improve usability and delight. Use when the user mentions adding animation, transitions, micro-interactions, motion design, hover effects, or making the UI feel more alive.

audit.description: Run technical quality checks across accessibility, performance, theming, responsive design, and anti-patterns. Generates a scored report with P0-P3 severity ratings, and in Optimize mode measures, fixes, and re-measures the largest performance bottleneck. Use for accessibility, performance, adaptation evidence, or technical quality review.

explore.description: Live UI testing that drives the running app and independently verifies every defect. An Explorer agent operates the real interface hunting failures across screen, console, network, and state; a structurally independent Verifier re-drives each candidate from a clean reset in its own browser and confirms or rejects it with its own evidence. Reports only confirmed defects, each as a replayable action log. Use when the user wants to test the real app, find what actually breaks, hunt bugs in a live browser, check for silent failures, or run exploratory UI testing. Web only; needs a running dev server and a Playwright MCP browser.

bolder.description: Amplify safe or boring designs, add one earned moment of delight, or push a selected target into a disciplined Overdrive implementation. Keeps scope and the incumbent world fixed while raising conviction, product-specific character, and technical ambition without sacrificing usability.

clarify.description: Improve unclear UX copy, error messages, labels, instructions, onboarding language, and first-value states. Reads the whole interaction path, keeps factual meaning and product terminology, and makes every state explain what happened and what the user can do next.

colorize.description: Add strategic color to features that are too monochromatic or lack visual interest, making interfaces more engaging and expressive. Use when the user mentions the design looking gray, dull, lacking warmth, needing more color, or wanting a more vibrant or expressive palette.

critique.description: Evaluate design from a UX perspective, assessing visual hierarchy, information architecture, emotional resonance, cognitive load, and overall quality with quantitative scoring, persona-based testing, automated anti-pattern detection, and actionable feedback. Use when the user asks to review, critique, evaluate, or give feedback on a design or component.

handdrawn.description: Draw a mascot, spot illustration, annotation mark or sketch diagram as clean hand-authored SVG. Builds tapered filled paths with deliberate line-weight variation, checks the drawing at its actual display size, and supports draw-on animation and reduced motion. Uses image tools only for construction references and diagnosis; the delivered asset remains editable vector geometry.

harden.description: Make interfaces production-ready: error handling, i18n, text overflow, edge case management, and resilience under real-world data. Use when the user asks to harden, make production-ready, handle edge cases, add error states, or fix overflow and i18n issues.

layout.description: Improve layout, spacing, and visual rhythm. Fixes monotonous grids, inconsistent spacing, and weak visual hierarchy. Use when the user mentions layout feeling off, spacing issues, visual hierarchy, crowded UI, alignment problems, or wanting better composition.

polish.description: Performs a final quality pass fixing alignment, spacing, consistency, and micro-detail issues before shipping. Use when the user mentions polish, finishing touches, pre-launch review, something looks off, or wants to go from good to great.

quieter.description: Tones down visually aggressive or overstimulating designs, reducing intensity while preserving quality. Use when the user mentions too bold, too loud, overwhelming, aggressive, garish, or wants a calmer, more refined aesthetic.

study.description: Read a design the user admires, given as a URL or a screenshot, and report its design DNA: page macrostructure, navigation and footer archetype, type pairing, colour anchor and dose, spacing rhythm, motion stance, the one device that makes it recognisable, and what it refuses. Diagnosis first, then optionally build in that language or lock it into a portable design system. Use when the user shares a site or a screenshot and asks what makes it work, how to get that look, or wants a reference captured. Describes a design language; never reproduces the source.

shape.description: Plan UX and UI before code. Runs a required multi-round discovery interview, uses visual probes when available, and produces a user-confirmed design brief for implementation.

typeset.description: Improves typography by fixing font choices, hierarchy, sizing, weight, and readability so text feels intentional. Use when the user mentions fonts, type, readability, text hierarchy, sizing looks off, or wants more polished, intentional typography.
